audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases is never mentioned anywhere in the matchup, and it is the single interaction that decides every Pantheon all-in into Mundo.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Dr. Mundo resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, instead losing Health and dropping a chemical cannister nearby. Dr. Mundo can pick it up by walking over it, restoring Health and reducing this Ability's Cooldown.' Shield Vault's stun is an immobilizing effect, so your entire opening is absorbed for free the first time — and if he collects the cannister he heals and gets the passive back sooner. The page currently promises a stun that does not land.
audit.corrected: Strip the passive with a cheap stun or your jungler's CC first, then commit; and fight him away from the dropped cannister so he cannot heal off it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heart Zapper is named as the focus ability but described only as a 'sustain spike + reset'. What it actually does inverts the burst plan.
audit.why: Riot's text: it deals persistent damage nearby while 'storing a portion of damage he takes', and on recast, if the burst hits, 'he heals a percentage of the stored damage'. Dumping a full Pantheon combo into an active Heart Zapper is how you pay for his heal. It is 17s at rank 1 against Shield Vault's 13s.
audit.corrected: Do not spend the burst into an active Heart Zapper — the damage you store is what he heals back. Commit inside its 17s downtime.

audit.whatIsWrong: Coverage flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere', and Blunt Force Trauma and Infected Bonesaw are never named.
audit.why: Heart Zapper 17/16.5/16/15.5/15, Infected Bonesaw 4s at 975, Blunt Force Trauma 9/8.25/7.5/6.75/6, Maximum Dosage a flat 120s. Bonesaw scales off your CURRENT health, not a flat percent, and Blunt Force Trauma scales off HIS MISSING health — so he gets stronger exactly as you win the trade.
audit.corrected: Real names and numbers throughout; the two scaling directions stated explicitly.

audit.why: 48.89% over 1080 games is the only losing matchup in this slice and the chart matches it — Pantheon takes levels 1-2, everything from 6 onward is Mundo's. The lane is a race against Maximum Dosage.

winCon already opens with 'Anti-heal', which is correct and load-bearing: Heart Zapper heals off stored damage, Maximum Dosage heals a percent of missing health, and the passive heals off the cannister. Grievous Wounds is not optional here.

edits.before: Mundo is one of the weakest early-game laners and you are one of the strongest, so press it. At Level 1 your point-and-click W stun plus a tap-Q does damage he simply cannot answer or escape. Use E to block his Q cleaver — that directional shield eats his only real poke, then W-in and tap-Q reset while his passive heal is still pathetic. Don't waste a held long-range Q on a 1000+ HP champ; tap it for trades and resets. Every chunk you land before he has items is permanent lead.
edits.after: Mundo is one of the weakest early laners and you are one of the strongest, so press it — but know that Goes Where He Pleases resists your FIRST stun outright and drops a cannister he heals off. Strip it with a throwaway Shield Vault or a jungle gank, then commit for real. Face his Infected Bonesaw so Aegis Assault eats it on its 4-second cooldown, and tap Comet Spear rather than holding it — a held spear is wasted on a health bar that size. Every chunk before his first item is permanent lead.

edits.before: Through 4-5 you still control the lane with empowered-Q poke and E blocks, but his passive sustain and self-heal start erasing chip you don't commit to a real all-in. At 6 your Grand Starfall is built for cross-map roams, not killing a 6th-level Mundo who just healed — so use R to make plays bot/mid instead of forcing a futile lane all-in. The clock is against you: his first HP item is coming and that flips the trade math, so cash your tempo into roams and objectives now.
edits.after: Through 4-5 you still control the lane, but stop dumping burst into an active Heart Zapper: it stores the damage you deal him and heals a share of it back on the recast. Commit inside its 17-second downtime instead. At 6 Maximum Dosage instantly heals a percent of his missing health on a flat 120 seconds, so Grand Starfall is a cross-map roam here and never a finisher. His first HP item flips the trade math — cash your tempo into roams and objectives now, while you still out-damage him.

edits.before: At Level 1 your point-and-click W stun plus tap-Q out-damages a Mundo who has no escape and a near-zero passive heal.
edits.after: At level 1 Shield Vault plus a tap-Q out-damages Mundo — though his passive resists the very first stun you land on him.

edits.after: With all three basics you face Infected Bonesaw, W-stun and tap-Q reset — but Heart Zapper heals back a share of whatever you store in it, so it is a skill window.

notes: _missing-interactions.json claims 'Dr. Mundo can cancel your Aegis Assault (E) with Goes Where He Pleases (P)'. That is backwards — his passive RESISTS incoming immobilizing effects, it does not apply any, so it cannot interrupt a channel. Logged in unverified rather than written. The genuinely missing mechanic was the same passive read correctly: it eats your first Shield Vault stun for free, which nothing on the page said. Also worth the user's attention: 'percent-HP poke' for Infected Bonesaw is loose — Riot's text says damage 'based on their current health', which is why the poke stops mattering once you are already low.
